intro: Query parameters can repeat, so parsing into a single value per key loses information. A multimap preserves repeated filters and their order.
task: Decode repeated query parameters into ordered value lists, retaining blank values.
requirements: Parse a query string without a leading ?. Separate pairs with &, split the first =, and treat absent = as a blank value. Decode + as space and percent escapes as strict UTF-8. Reject malformed percent escapes and empty decoded keys. Return each key mapped to values in occurrence order; ignore empty & segments.
Text inputs contain valid Unicode scalar characters and at most 10000 characters. Identifier and dictionary keys are nonempty strings of at most 100 characters.
Return the documented Python output types and preserve all caller inputs. Raise ValueError for invalid inputs unless the task explicitly reports a record-level rejection.

hints.title: Trace one record
hints.body: Decode key and value after splitting the structural separators.

hints.title: Handle the boundary
hints.body: Keep repeated values in lists; a plain dictionary assignment would lose earlier values.

explanation: Query parameters can repeat, so parsing into a single value per key loses information. A multimap preserves repeated filters and their order.
Decoding happens after structural splitting because an encoded ampersand belongs inside a value. Strict percent and UTF-8 validation avoids silently replacing malformed data.
